Eicosanoids
Eicosanoids, derived from fatty acids, play roles in cell signaling and inflammation, with n-6 and n-3
fatty acids yielding different physiological effects.
Alcohol
Metabolism
Ethanol is metabolized via alcohol dehydrogenase and the MEOS. High consumption can cause
metabolic issues, including fatty liver from increased NADH and altered lipid synthesis.
Cholesterol
Synthesis and
Regulation
Cholesterol is synthesized from acetyl-CoA, with homeostasis maintained through feedback inhibition,
particularly on HMG-CoA reductase.
Conclusion
Understanding lipid metabolism, especially concerning fatty acids, alcohol, and cholesterol, is crucial for
addressing cardiovascular disease and health issues.


Chapter 5 Summary: Lipids
Definition and Importance of Lipids
  
Lipids are distinguished by their solubility in organic
solvents like ether and chloroform. They serve various
functions in the body, including energy provision, structural
components of cell membranes, fat-soluble vitamins, and
hormones. This chapter focuses on lipids relevant to energy
metabolism.
